_comment: Haiku selection bench fixtures — conversation-behavior scenarios the frozen-corpus sweep cannot exercise (its queries are single-shot). Each scenario: frame + turns (with per-turn surfaced) + current message + candidates + expected picks. Candidates are compact node dicts in the shape build_surface_prompt renders. Scoring: every must_pick id picked, no must_not_pick id picked, total picks <= max_picks.

scenarios.name: shown_repick_trap
scenarios.notes: The strongest on-topic candidate was ALREADY shown last turn. Haiku must not re-pick it; the fresh detail candidate is the right pick.
scenarios.frame:
## Current focus
Debugging the deploy pipeline timeout

turns.content: the deploy keeps timing out on staging

surfaced.title: Deploy timeout root cause: staging ALB health-check interval too aggressive

turns.content: That matches the ALB health-check finding — staging checks every 5s while the app needs 8s to warm.

scenarios.current_message: so whats the actual fix for the timeout?

candidates.title: Deploy timeout root cause: staging ALB health-check interval too aggressive
candidates.content: Staging ALB health-check interval is 5s; app warmup needs 8s. Root cause of the deploy timeouts.

candidates.title: Fix chosen: raise staging health-check interval to 15s + add /ready endpoint
candidates.content: Decision: raise the staging ALB health-check interval to 15s and add a lightweight /ready endpoint so warmup no longer fails checks.

candidates.title: Production deploy window is Tuesday mornings
candidates.content: Deploys to production happen Tuesday mornings after standup.

scenarios.name: current_vs_history
scenarios.notes: History is all about topic A (recall latency); the current message pivots to topic B (dashboard auth). Picks must serve B, not the louder history topic.

turns.content: recall latency is spiking again, p95 over 2 seconds
The spike correlates with the embedder cold starts — same pattern as last week.
ok lets look at the embedder warm pool then
Warm pool sizing is 2 workers; bumping to 4 would cover the p95 spike window.

scenarios.current_message: different thing — why does the dashboard ask me to log in every day?

candidates.title: Recall p95 spike traced to embedder cold starts
candidates.content: The p95 latency spikes correlate with embedder cold starts after idle periods.

candidates.title: Dashboard session cookie expiry set to 24h — intentional security default
candidates.content: The dashboard session cookie expires after 24h by design; the operator asked for a security-conservative default until SSO lands.

candidates.title: Embedder warm pool: 2 workers, 90s idle recycle
candidates.content: The embedder keeps 2 warm workers and recycles them after 90s idle.

scenarios.name: vague_referent_from_thread
scenarios.notes: Current message says 'that bug' — resolvable only from turn 1 (the WAL checkpoint stall). The right pick is the WAL bug node, not the generically-worded bug node.

turns.content: the WAL checkpoint stall hit us again on the logs db
Confirmed — checkpoint blocked 40s during the trace flush. Same signature as the June incident.

scenarios.current_message: did we ever write down the workaround for that bug?

candidates.title: WAL checkpoint stall on logs db during trace flush — workaround: passive checkpoint + flush batching
candidates.content: WAL checkpoint stalls when trace flush holds the reader. Workaround: switch to passive checkpoints and batch the flush.

candidates.title: Dashboard graph render bug: labels overlap at high zoom
candidates.content: Graph labels overlap at zoom >2x. Cosmetic.

candidates.title: Bugs found late in session tend to be encoding-side, not recall-side
candidates.content: Pattern: late-session bugs cluster on the encode path.

scenarios.name: duplicate_information_one_pick
scenarios.notes: Two candidates carry the same fact in different words; picking both wastes a slot. Exactly one of the pair plus the complementary node.

turns.content: planning the migration window for the schema change
The v30 migration needs the maintenance lock and a backup first.

scenarios.current_message: remind me what the migration protocol requires?

candidates.title: Schema migrations require maintenance lock + pre-migration backup
candidates.content: Before any schema migration: touch the maintenance lock, back up brain.db, then migrate.

candidates.title: Always backup brain.db and hold the maintenance lock before migrating schemas
candidates.content: Migration protocol: maintenance lock on, cp brain.db backup, run migration, verify, release lock.

candidates.title: Migration v22 lesson: restart the daemon only after WAL checkpoint completes
candidates.content: v22 migration hung because the daemon restarted mid-checkpoint; wait for checkpoint completion.

scenarios.name: fresh_session_no_history
scenarios.notes: First message of a session — empty conversation. Sanity: normal on-topic pick still works with no history.
scenarios.current_message: where did we land on the edge weight question?

candidates.title: Edge weight is dead — static 0.5; rank on edge_relations cosine instead
candidates.content: Weight on edges is a static 0.5 and must never be ranked on; edge relevance comes from cosine against edge_relations.embedding.

candidates.title: Graph has ~7000 nodes as of July
candidates.content: Node count crossed 7000 in early July.

scenarios.name: shown_two_turns_back
scenarios.notes: A memory shown two turns ago (not the immediately previous turn) is still out of scope. Tests window-wide shown adherence, not just last-turn.

turns.content: why does consolidation keep skipping cluster 7?

surfaced.title: Cluster 7 skip: fingerprint suppression after three SKIP verdicts

turns.content: Cluster 7 got fingerprint-suppressed after three SKIP verdicts — it will re-propose when the graph changes.
makes sense, and the healer?
Healer is idle-gated; it stamps its own last-run timestamp and skips unchanged graphs.

scenarios.current_message: back to consolidation — is cluster 7 permanently blocked then?

candidates.title: Cluster 7 skip: fingerprint suppression after three SKIP verdicts
candidates.content: Cluster 7 was fingerprint-suppressed after three SKIP verdicts from the encoder.

candidates.title: Fingerprint suppression is state-conditional — legitimate re-proposals pass when graph state changes
candidates.content: s2_rejections stores input fingerprints; when a cluster's meaningful inputs change, the fingerprint no longer matches and the proposal passes again. Suppression is never permanent.
